subject: Maths
title: 6, 7, 9, 11, 12 times tables
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (Times Tables to 12×12) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can recall the harder times tables (6, 7, 9, 11, 12) and use them to solve problems.

key_vocab.definition: The 9 times table trick: the digits of every multiple of 9 add to 9 (e.g. 36 → 3+6 = 9). Or use 10×n then subtract n: 9×7 = 70 − 7 = 63.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can recall the harder times tables (6, 7, 9, 11, 12) and use them to solve problems.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: 9 times table -- The 9 times table trick: the digits of every multiple of 9 add to 9 (e.g. 36 → 3+6 = 9). Or use 10×n then subtract n: 9×7 = 70 − 7 = 63.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Use friendly facts to bridge to harder ones. e.g. 7×6 = (7×5) + 7 = 35 + 7 = 42.
9 × 8 = 10 × 8 − 8 = 72
×10 then subtract

Key examples:
  ✓ 9 × 7 = 63 (6+3=9)  (9-trick)
  ✓ 11 × 5 = 55  (doubled digit)
  ✓ 12 × 6 = 72  (double 6 = 12, ×6 = 72)
  ✗ 7 × 8 = 54  (should be 56)
  ✗ 11 × 12 = 121  (should be 132)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – 9 times table trick
  Calculate 9 × 6
  10 × 6 = 60
  Subtract one 6
  60 − 6 = 54
  = 54
  (Multiples of 9 are always one less than 10×n.)

Example 2 – 7 times table
  Calculate 7 × 8
  7 × 7 = 49
  Add one more 7
  49 + 7 = 56
  = 56
  (Use the square fact 7×7=49 as a stepping stone.)

sections.title: 11 times table
sections.content:
Most are easy — just repeat the digit. Watch out for 11×10, 11×11, 11×12!
